mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engine replacement typically costs between £4,500 and £6,500 for a rebuilt N55B30A unit. The hybrid system adds complexity, so ensure your quote includes the engine only or the full hybrid system as required. Used BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engines: £2,200-£3,800. Reconditioned BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engines: £3,800-£5,500. Rebuilt BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engines: £4,500-£6,500.

mainEntity.name: Does the BMW ActiveHybrid 3 have timing chain issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N55 engine in the BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 does not suffer from the catastrophic timing chain failures of older BMW engines like the N47 or N20. The N55's timing chain is front-mounted and generally reliable. The main N55 weaknesses are wastegate rattle, valve cover gasket leaks, and electric water pump failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the age, mileage and condition of your car. The ActiveHybrid 3 is a rare model - only 108 M Sport and 23 Luxury examples were registered in the UK. With typical values between £4,000-£9,000, a full engine replacement may not be cost-effective on higher-mileage examples. For low-mileage, well-maintained cars, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 engine replacement typically takes 12-16 labour hours for the N55B30A unit. The hybrid system integration means the high-voltage components must be handled with care - allow 3-5 working days for the complete job with a specialist. Supply only: engine can be delivered next working day. Supply & fit: allow 3-5 days for the complete job.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW ActiveHybrid 3 and 330e?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW ActiveHybrid 3 (2012-2013) is a full hybrid - it cannot be plugged in and has a small battery that is charged by the petrol engine and regenerative braking. The BMW 330e (2016 onwards) is a plug-in hybrid with a larger battery that can be charged from an external power source, offering a longer electric-only range. ActiveHybrid 3: 340 hp, 0-60 in 5.1 seconds, 47 mpg. 330e: up to 292 hp, 0-60 in 5.9 seconds, 134 mpg (plug-in capability).

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW ActiveHybrid 3 hybrid system?

acceptedAnswer.text: The hybrid system in the BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 has several known issues: battery pack degradation - reduced electric range and performance; hybrid system faults - warning lights, reduced performance; regenerative braking issues - inconsistent brake feel; and electric motor and power electronics failures.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW ActiveHybrid 3 arrived in 2012 as the first hybrid version of the 3 Series, combining the award-winning N55 3.0-litre twin-scroll turbo six-cylinder petrol engine from the 335i with a 40 kW electric motor. The result was 340 hp system output with 18% better fuel economy than the 335i - a genuine performance hybrid that could accelerate from 0-60 mph in 5.1 seconds while delivering 47 mpg.

milestones.description: N55B30A (306 hp petrol engine + 40 kW / 54 hp electric motor, 340 hp system output). Launched in the F30 ActiveHybrid 3 saloon.
Available in SE, Modern, Luxury and M Sport specification.
Production ends. The ActiveHybrid 3 was a short-lived model, replaced by the 330e plug-in hybrid in 2016. Only 108 M Sport examples and 23 Luxury examples were registered in the UK.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 is powered by the N55B30A 3.0-litre six-cylinder petrol engine - the same unit found in the 335i - paired with a 40 kW electric motor and a high-voltage lithium-ion battery. While the N55 is a robust and rewarding engine, it has well-documented weaknesses including wastegate rattle and oil leaks. The hybrid system adds further complexity: battery degradation and hybrid system faults are common concerns. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N55 Wastegate Rattle & Oil Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 N55 Needs Attention
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger wastegate can develop rattle due to wear in the wastegate arm bushing. Valve cover gasket and oil filter housing gasket leaks are common, leading to oil consumption and potential fire risk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbocharger or repair wastegate assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Essential if rattle is severe or boost is affected
When engine is already damaged or high-mileage rebuild needed

problems.recommendation: If you own a BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3, prioritise preventative maintenance - address oil leaks promptly and listen for wastegate rattle. The hybrid battery is the biggest long-term cost risk; if the car is worth under £5,000, battery reconditioning or a used engine is often more cost-effective than a full rebuild. For low-mileage, well-maintained examples, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment.

problems.h4: Hybrid Battery Degradation - Why the BMW 3 Series ActiveHybrid 3 Needs Attention
problems.rootCause: The high-voltage lithium-ion battery pack degrades over time, leading to reduced electric-only range, diminished performance, and increased reliance on the petrol engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Recondition or replace individual battery cells
repairOptions.longevity: If battery degradation is mild to moderate
If battery is severely degraded or has failed
If petrol engine fails - hybrid system may still be serviceable
